statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is elevated as the earlier post-speech rebound was followed by a delayed downside second leg with firmer Treasury yields and weaker technology.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. The elevated state would ease if meaningful retracements reappear and rates and technology stop reinforcing the downside path.
headline: Delayed post-Warsh second leg lifts Tail into the elevated band
body: The Nasdaq-100 was about 1% lower by 12:20 ET after an earlier rebound, while the 2-year Treasury yield was near 4.34%, the 10-year near 4.72%, and technology lagged. The failed rebound plus cross-asset alignment raises mean-reversion-failure risk, though direct live NQ path detail remains limited.

forecast.analysis: Elevated Tail persists conditionally if early-afternoon rebounds remain shallow while yields stay firm and technology keeps underperforming. A meaningful retracement and loss of cross-asset alignment would reduce the mean-reversion-failure signal.

Power hour is a second conditional amplification window. Tail rises within the elevated band if selling extends after failed rebounds and the index remains near session lows with rates and technology aligned; a broad recovery would invalidate that path.

Into the cash close, elevated Tail is conditional on persistent downside efficiency and weak closing breadth. If late positioning produces a two-way reversal, Tail should fall back below the block threshold.

After the cash close, Tail falls to low unless futures continue the downside leg without meaningful retracement into the Friday futures close. Stress remains elevated because late positioning can still create sharp but recoverable moves.

Once Friday index-futures trading ends, live path evidence disappears. Remaining risk shifts to verified weekend headlines and potential reopening gaps rather than an already-observed persistent trend.
